seat: Claude Opus 5.5, high effort, Agent-tool subagent (GPU)

disclosure_pre_registration_design_probe.what: Design probe P0 ran on the GPU BEFORE this registration. It is not a gate. It asked whether a composed engine-op rule can be bit-identical to BK4 at all, and it fixed no threshold (every threshold below is the order's).
findings_known_at_registration: An fp32 transcription of BK4's compiled arithmetic (SASS: FADD sums, FFMA squares, IEEE div, FFMA var and th), fed BK4's own WMMA dots (extracted through its thr output at S=L=1, scale 1, z 0), reproduces BK4 thr bits and mask exactly: 0/4096 rows and 0/33554432 mask entries (Qwen3-1.7B L16, L2048, bulk 8, 2 KV heads).

The engine's fp32 matmul (cublasSgemmStridedBatched) differs bitwise from BK4's bf16 WMMA dot in 25068385/33554432 entries. Even with a perfect transcription of the statistics on SGEMM dots, 2 mask entries differ from 'h'.
BK4 'h' and the shipped 'a' kernel disagree with each other on 15 mask entries and on 3980/4096 thr bit patterns in the same cell.

Seat expectation, therefore: G2 fp32 exactness vs 'h' is likely RED on large real cells. The residual is R1 (dot bits), which needs a kernel or engine change (out of scope). That is the order's stop-and-report rail.

definitions.visible: row i of L queries sees key j iff j <= S-L+i (bottom-right; 63960a4; Dao 2023). Non-causal: all j.
definitions.bk4_rule: kernels.cu:8064-8077,8112-8114: count_i = S-L+i+1 (causal) or S; a_ij = |fl32(dot_ij*scale)| over visible j; mean = sum a/count; var = max(sum a^2/count - mean^2, 0); th = mean + z*sqrt(var); sel = visible && a >= th. z = _norm_ppf(1-p).
definitions.kernel_masks: tc._C.bp_kernel_4_diagnostic(q,k,kq,v,scale,z,causal,variant)[3] for variant 'h' (bk4::forward, kernels.cu:8027) and 'a' (apa_selective_fwd_train + a_mask). Kernel thr = [2]. BF16 operands only (kernels.cu:8163).
definitions.identical_operands: q, k, kq, v are the same bf16 values for the kernel and the composed rule. kq is quant._quantize_keys of the bf16 K: bf16, the kernel's kq, as in MF1. The composed rule receives their exact fp32 upcasts.
definitions.fp32_item1_cell: The selection produced by quant.py's rule in fp32 arithmetic on identical operands. Realized (i) as the selection helper on fp32 tensors holding the bf16 values, and (ii) as apa_quant_attention on bf16 tensors (selection captured at the tc.where condition). (i) and (ii) must be identical (plumbing check, exact).
definitions.agreement: 1 - mismatches / (L*S*heads), over ALL L x S entries (visible and invisible); mismatches also reported over visible only. Gated vs 'h'; 'a' reported, not gated, because 'h' and 'a' disagree with each other (P0).
definitions.tie_band: |a - thr| <= 2e-5*max(1,|thr|), thr = kernel thr ('h') where a kernel exists, else my fp64 oracle thr.
definitions.oracle: scripts/apa_mf2_bk4emu.py rule_fp64: fp64 numpy written from the definition. It never imports MF1's or the reviewer's helpers.

gates.G1: tensor_cuda/tests full suite: python3 -m pytest tensor_cuda/tests -q -p no:cacheprovider --ignore=tensor_cuda/tests/test_selector_accuracy.py -rfE. The FAILED/ERROR id set must equal the 52 ids in tensor_fork_apa_wt_mf1/logs/apa_mf1_g1_baseline_unchanged.log. test_apa_phase6::test_apa_causal must PASS. New tensor_cuda/tests/test_apa_mf2_*.py run as part of the suite and must pass. apa_cuda tests: pass/skip/fail counts equal or improved vs before (same environment).

G2.G2a_fp32_exact: In every real cell (36) and every synthetic cell (72), the fp32 item-1 selection equals the 'h' diagnostic mask exactly: mismatches == 0, agreement == 1.0. No tie band.
G2.G2b_bf16_fp16_band: apa_quant_attention on bf16 operands vs 'h' (identical operands), and on fp16 operands vs the fp64 oracle on the call's own operands (no fp16 kernel exists): every mismatch lies inside the tie band, and all are counted.
G2.G2c_review_cases: B1, B2 and B3 are RED on before (MF1 A+B) and GREEN on after. GREEN means the after selection equals the 'h' kernel mask on the case's operands. For B3 that is exactly 24 selected entries, all visible.
G2.plumbing: (i) == (ii) exactly in every synthetic and real cell.

G3.leak: On after, every query row that cannot see the adversarial key gets output exactly 0.0 (bitwise) for every M, dtype, shape and path. Rows that can see it stay finite. Before (fd32b6d and MF1 A+B) is expected RED for M large enough to beat the bias.
G3.byte_identity: Every realistic arm in census.byte_identity_real is bytewise equal, before vs after (outputs; SDPA grad-on also dq/dk/dv). GRM Qwen3-1.7B standard-mode logits are bytewise equal, before functional vs after functional, on one wikitext-2 window: prefill 8192 tokens in 512-token chunks, then 32 teacher-forced steps. The GRAPA GQAAttention forward is bytewise equal before vs after on small real-shaped inputs (refine 1.0 SDPA path and the force_selective composed path; grad on and off), GRAPA imported read-only.
G3.finite: No NaN or Inf in any S >= L output of the above (after arm).
